candidates.change_summary: Replace `require(msg.value == 10 ether);` with `require(msg.value == 1 ether);` to change the payment threshold, causing different revert behavior and balance transfers.
Delete `require(msg.value == 10 ether);` to allow calls with any msg.value, changing when the fallback reverts and potentially altering subsequent balance transfers.

Replace `require(block.timestamp > pastBlockTime);` with `require(block.timestamp >= pastBlockTime);` to allow a call in the same block timestamp, changing revert conditions and thus externally observable behavior.
Delete `require(block.timestamp > pastBlockTime);` to remove the timestamp check, allowing multiple calls in the same block and changing the revert surface.
Delete `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;` so that the timestamp check only passes once, changing the external revert behavior for subsequent calls.
Replace `if(block.number % 15 == 0)` with `if(block.number % 15 != 0)` to invert the condition for transferring the balance, directly changing the transfer behavior.
Delete the entire if-block `if(block.number % 15 == 0) { payable(msg.sender).transfer(address(this).balance); }` to stop balance transfers, changing the contract's balance and ETH flow.
Replace `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;` with `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp + 1;` to set the stored timestamp one second ahead, altering future timestamp check outcomes.
Move `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;` before `require(block.timestamp > pastBlockTime);` so the check is against the new timestamp instead of the old one, always failing the require.
